PDF 328–350，{'theme': 'Chapter 3 title, Single-Particle Configurations.', 'pages': [328, 328]}；{'theme': 'Spherical closed-shell model, radial and spin-angular wave functions, coupling of orbital and spin angular momenta, and spin projection along the radius vector. PDF 364–397，{'theme': 'Allowed β-decay theory uses the long-lepton-wavelength limit and neglects nucleon position and velocity in the transition operators. Mirror decays test the single-particle estimate for spin-saturated N = Z cores.', 'pdf_interval': [364, 365]}；{'theme': 'For neutron-rich cores, same-orbit charge exchange is degenerate with corresponding core transitions in the model. Spin–isospin correlations shift Gamow–Teller strength toward a higher collective excitation. Exact supermultiplet selection rules require a spin- and charge-independent interaction. The text identifies strong spin–orbit splitting as a source of symmetry breaking.', 'pdf_interval': [366, 367]}

PDF 414–440，{'theme': 'Weak processes classified as purely leptonic, semileptonic, or purely hadronic. A local current–current coupling provides a common framework, and a massive intermediate vector field is considered as a hypothesis.', 'pdf_interval': [414, 417]}；{'theme': 'Historical evidence for separate electron and muon lepton numbers, including neutrino-induced reactions and tellurium-ore evidence for double beta decay. The isotope labels and half-life exponent in the ore example contain OCR errors.', 'pdf_interval': [416, 417]}

PDF 441–467，{'theme': 'Single-nucleon transfer amplitudes. Stripping and pickup use creation and annihilation matrix elements related by time reversal. A radial overlap replaces the fixed-orbital approximation when the transferred nucleon has a substantially different binding energy. Deformed targets can be treated in the intrinsic frame.', 'pages': [441, 442]}；{'theme': 'Transfer cross sections and sum rules. Unpolarized sums add contributions from different j values incoherently, while angular correlations can require coherent amplitudes. The text distinguishes summed and averaged single-particle normalizations, introduces isospin coupling, and derives occupancy and vacancy sums. OCR error obscures parts of the phase, normalization, and tensor-recoupling formulas.', 'pages': [442, 443]}

PDF 187–212，{'theme': 'Exercise 6.10 compares spherical and deformation-dependent rigid-body inertia terms with a reported experimental comparison factor of 3.88. OCR errors obscure the formula, numerical prefactor, and isotope symbol.', 'pdf_pages': [187, 187]}；{'theme': 'Wilets–Jean γ instability gives a ring of minima at finite β, with β stiffness, equilibrium deformation, well depth, and collective mass as parameters. K mixing leads to separable shape dynamics and β-phonon bands classified by seniority. OCR errors obscure the exact Hamiltonian, energy formulas, centrifugal power, and parts of the level diagram.', 'pdf_pages': [187, 189]}

PDF 213–241，{'theme': 'Theory. IBA2 assigns separate proton and neutron s and d bosons. Its simplified Hamiltonian counts d bosons by species and includes like-boson, proton–neutron quadrupole, and Majorana interactions. OCR error obscures several tensor coefficients.', 'pdf_pages': [213, 214]}；{'theme': 'Reported experimental evidence. The book places mixed-symmetry states near 3 MeV. It interprets them geometrically as relative oscillations of the proton and neutron surfaces.', 'pdf_pages': [214, 214]}

PDF 242–273，{'theme': 'Theory. Hartree–Fock varies a Slater determinant. The occupied orbitals generate a direct density potential and a nonlocal exchange term, and the resulting field determines the orbitals in the next iteration. The text invokes Pauli blocking to justify neglecting some correlations and assigns pairing and correlated excitations to the residual interaction.', 'pdf_pages': [242, 243]}；{'theme': 'Exercise 7.2. Evaluates kinetic and two-body matrix elements by moving creation and annihilation operators through the occupied determinant. The surviving number-operator expectation restricts the final sum to occupied states. OCR error obscures detailed subscripts and contractions.', 'pdf_pages': [243, 244]}

PDF 274–304，{'theme': 'Exercise 7.6 derives spin–orbit matrix elements for an axially deformed oscillator. The cylindrical basis diagonalizes the oscillator, while the spherical basis diagonalizes the spin–orbit term. The exercise factors the axial, radial, azimuthal and spin integrals, uses Laguerre orthogonality and recurrences, and builds sparse blocks of fixed angular-momentum projection. The 15-state example illustrates truncation and convergence checks.', 'pages': [274, 278]}；{'theme': 'Exercise 7.7 models an avoided crossing with two linear levels and a constant off-diagonal interaction. It follows the exchange of wave-function character and connects slow passage through the crossing to quadrupole motion.', 'pages': [278, 279]}

PDF 305–336，{'theme': 'Theory. The real Bogolyubov transformation preserves the fermionic anticommutators. Normal ordering the particle-number-constrained Hamiltonian isolates the vacuum energy, the quasiparticle term and the pair creation and annihilation terms. Canceling the last two gives the Hartree–Fock–Bogolyubov (HFB) condition, which reduces to Hartree–Fock for occupations restricted to 0 or 1.', 'pages': [305, 307]}；{'theme': 'Theory. A diagonal pairing field gives a gap for each orbital. The simple BCS limit uses a constant pairing interaction with matrix-element sign −G. The occupation probabilities feed back into the single-particle field. In the independent-quasiparticle approximation, even-nucleus excitations use sums of two quasiparticle energies, while odd-nucleus excitations use differences. Only the vacuum has a constrained mean particle number.', 'pages': [307, 309]}

PDF 337–368，{'theme': 'Theory. Collective kinetic energy is quadratic and local in time, with deformation-dependent inertia and possible off-diagonal couplings. The text discusses friction as a way to describe dissipation that complicates quantization.', 'pdf_pages': [337, 337]}；{'theme': 'Theory. Liquid-drop deformation energy balances rising surface energy against falling Coulomb energy. Quadrupole stability reaches its threshold at fissility x = 1, corresponding to a critical Z²/A of about 50. The text gives roughly 12 MeV for the uranium liquid-drop barrier and 6 MeV after shell correction.', 'pdf_pages': [337, 339]}

PDF 369–399，{'theme': 'Generator-coordinate theory. The square root of the overlap kernel converts the Hill–Wheeler–Griffin weight into a conventionally normalized collective wave function. A narrow Gaussian overlap then permits a second-order expansion and a local differential Hamiltonian. OCR errors obscure the Gaussian exponent, several expansion coefficients and signs, and the explicit collective mass formula.', 'pdf_pages': [369, 372]}；{'theme': 'Reported modern observations. Heavy-ion reactions reach spins of order 60, with the unit glyph corrupted by OCR. The text reports evidence for superdeformation through closely spaced rotational bands. Fig. 9.18 gives a usual experimental backbending range of 10–20 in angular momentum and presents a schematic band crossing.', 'pdf_pages': [372, 373]}

PDF 72–100，{'theme': 'Electron stopping. Møller ionization loss accounts for finite collision masses and exchange between indistinguishable electrons. The low-speed approximation gives −dE/dx proportional to 1/v² when the bracketed term varies slowly. Bremsstrahlung grows with electron energy and absorber Z, and the text places it near parity with ionization for 9 MeV electrons in lead. OCR obscures parts of the stopping equations and the silicon comparison.', 'pdf_interval': [72, 72]}；{'theme': 'Electron scattering and empirical absorption data. High-Z backing can return β electrons to the detector and raise the count. The straight part of the 1.9 MeV monoenergetic electron transmission curve is extrapolated to zero to define a range. A continuous β spectrum is treated through empirical attenuation against mass thickness. OCR damages the β mass-absorption coefficient in Eq. (3.1-18).', 'pdf_interval': [72, 73]}

PDF 101–126，{'pdf_interval': [101, 101], 'theme': 'Detector energy resolution combines fluctuations in primary signal production, charge collection or multiplication, and electronic noise. The book gives about 3 eV per pair in Si, about 30 eV in noble gases, and 300–500 eV of deposited energy per photoelectron collected at a scintillation photomultiplier’s first dynode. OCR error obscures the exact form of Eq. (3.3-3).'}；{'pdf_interval': [101, 102], 'theme': 'A single γ spectrum with 200 and 300 keV lines fits two level schemes. Energy-selective γ–γ coincidence distinguishes a prompt cascade by testing whether both lines occur within the resolving interval. OCR error obscures several timing and count-rate exponents in the worked examples.'}

PDF 165–202，{'theme': 'Allowed K-shell electron capture. The derivation uses a bound K electron, a plane-wave neutrino with Eν = cpν, and a point nuclear charge. It counts two K-shell electrons and evaluates the final-state density at the discrete neutrino energy. For the same nuclear transition, the K-capture to β⁺ rate ratio cancels the nuclear matrix element. The text gives 1.022 MeV as the atomic mass-energy threshold above which β⁺ emission can compete.', 'pdf_interval': [165, 166]}；{'theme': 'Reported comparison of theoretical and measured K-capture to β⁺ ratios in Table 6-5. OCR obscures several nuclide labels and the ratio scale in the table headings.', 'pdf_interval': [166, 166]}

PDF 203–233，{'theme': 'Theory. Atomic shell filling and Pauli capacities motivate separate proton and neutron shells in a mean field generated by the other nucleons. For nearly spherical nuclei the field is treated as central. Pauli blocking suppresses scattering into occupied states, supporting the independent-particle approximation.', 'pages': [203, 204]}；{'theme': 'Theory. The spherical square well and harmonic oscillator are calculable limits. The book favors a Woods–Saxon potential for the nuclear surface and interpolates between the simpler spectra. OCR error obscures the printed Woods–Saxon expression.', 'pages': [204, 206]}

PDF 234–266，{'theme': 'Reported experimental background and §8.8 models. The text describes strong short-range repulsion at about 0.5 fm and pointlike constituents seen in deep-inelastic scattering. It models the nucleon as a spherical quark bag, retains meson exchange for longer-range nuclear forces, and presents a six-quark dibaryon as a prediction awaiting experimental confirmation. OCR error on PDF 234 obscures parts of the bag-energy equation and the hyperon label.', 'pdf_interval': [234, 234]}；{'theme': 'Quark–gluon plasma theory. The two pressure-balance estimates use a hot gas at zero net baryon number and a cold, degenerate quark gas. Figure 8-32 sketches the intervening regime. OCR errors on PDF 235–236 obscure some formula terms, density-unit exponents, and figure labels.', 'pdf_interval': [234, 236]}

PDF 267–299，{'theme': 'Optical model. Feshbach’s complex square well −(V₀ + iW), with V₀ = 42 MeV, treats absorption through the imaginary potential. The text then describes a Woods–Saxon fit with surface diffuseness, spin–orbit coupling, and surface-localized absorption for low-energy particles. OCR errors obscure the radius exponent and parts of the displayed formulas.', 'pdf_interval': [267, 269]}；{'theme': 'Reported optical-model comparisons. The neutron total cross section varies with energy and target mass number, with broad oscillations the text calls giant resonances. The 30.3 MeV proton elastic-scattering data are plotted as a ratio to Rutherford scattering against center-of-mass angle. Table 9-1 gives fitted proton optical-potential parameters.', 'pdf_interval': [267, 269]}

PDF 300–331，{'theme': 'Reported radioactive-beam production results. Proton-induced spallation and heavy-ion projectile fragmentation are compared using rubidium isotope yields on uranium and oxygen fragmentation on beryllium. OCR error obscures several isotope superscripts and graph scales.', 'pages': [300, 300]}；{'theme': 'Radioactive-beam preparation by ISOL with post-acceleration and by in-flight projectile-fragment separation. The book compares intensity, beam quality, release time and chemical dependence. OCR error obscures the short-lifetime unit and the inequality near 20 MeV/A.', 'pages': [301, 301]}

PDF 332–366，{'theme': 'Reported fission-fragment total kinetic energies in MeV, Table 11-4. OCR error affects several isotope labels and uncertainty signs.', 'pdf_interval': [332, 332]}；{'theme': 'Prompt fission-neutron spectra and multiplicities. The text fits the continuous laboratory-frame spectrum with a one-parameter Maxwell distribution, gives a typical mean energy of about 2 MeV, and compares multiplicity data with a Gaussian. The angular distributions support evaporation from accelerated fragments, with a smaller contribution attributed to scission. OCR error affects isotope labels, the Terrell formula, and parts of the multiplicity table.', 'pdf_interval': [332, 334]}

PDF 367–399，{'theme': 'Historical accelerator survey covering beam energies, luminosities and research programs. The book projects staged LHC operation in 2005–2008 with proton beams of 2 × 7 TeV. OCR error obscures several luminosity exponents and unit superscripts.', 'pdf_interval': [367, 367]}；{'theme': 'Pion charge and isospin triplet, mass measurements, spin from detailed balance, and intrinsic parity from low-energy capture. The decay treatment combines two-body phase space and helicity suppression to predict an electron-to-muon decay-rate ratio of 1.28 × 10⁻⁴. OCR error affects the neutral-pion lifetime exponent, some decay channels and intermediate equations.', 'pdf_interval': [367, 370]}

PDF 400–439，{'theme': 'Charge conjugation, G parity as charge conjugation combined with a 180° isospin rotation, and CPT invariance for local Lorentz-invariant interactions. The book discusses neutral-kaon CP violation and particle–antiparticle tests of CPT. OCR error obscures the two-particle C-parity exponent.', 'pdf_pages': [400, 400]}；{'theme': 'The Standard Model combines electroweak gauge theory and QCD. The text explains Higgs mass generation through spontaneous symmetry breaking and identifies unresolved questions about three generations, measured input parameters, and left–right asymmetry. The 2 × 7 TeV proton–proton LHC is described as a future experiment. OCR error damages the luminosity and Higgs mass-unit exponents.', 'pdf_pages': [400, 401]}

PDF 49–78，{'theme': 'Theory of nine quadric surfaces in suitably chosen Cartesian coordinates. Horizontal sections of the elliptic cone are similar ellipses that shrink to the vertex at z=0. Rotation and axial scaling generate several other quadrics. The saddle is built by translating downward-opening parabolas along a parabolic directrix. OCR errors obscure several standard equations and scale factors.', 'pdf_interval': [49, 51]}；{'theme': 'Exercises 8-5 on spheres, surfaces of revolution, quadric identification, and solids bounded by surfaces. OCR errors obscure parts of several equations.', 'pdf_interval': [51, 52]}

PDF 79–108，{'theme': 'Total increment and total differential. Differentiability is defined by a linear approximation with a little-o remainder. The text proves the necessary and sufficient conditions it states separately and gives a counterexample with both partial derivatives zero at the origin.', 'pdf_pages': [79, 82]}；{'theme': 'First-order approximation and error limits. For small input errors, the absolute error estimate weights each input error limit by the magnitude of its partial derivative. The relative estimate divides by the magnitude of the nominal output when it is nonzero. Worked examples give a cylinder volume change of approximately −200π cm³ for Δr = +0.05 cm and Δh = −1 cm, and a pendulum estimate of about 4.93 cm/s² absolute error and 0.5% relative error.', 'pdf_pages': [82, 84]}

PDF 109–137，{'pages': [109, 109], 'theme': 'Worked tangent-plane and normal-line examples use normals (2, 4, 6) for the sphere and (4, 2, −1) for the paraboloid. The resulting planes are x + 2y + 3z − 14 = 0 and 4x + 2y − z − 6 = 0. OCR error obscures the opening direction-cosine formulas.'}；{'pages': [109, 110], 'theme': 'Exercises 9-6 cover vector limits and differentiation, particle velocity and acceleration, curve tangents and normal planes, and surface tangent planes and normals. OCR error obscures several exact hypotheses and equations.'}

PDF 138–180，{'theme': 'Exponential least squares. A common-log plot motivates a straight-line fit, and an eight-observation table supplies the sums for the two normal equations.', 'pdf_interval': [138, 139]}；{'theme': "Least-squares exercises on an affine fit to tabulated observations and the three normal equations for a quadratic fit. The first table preserves p/% but has an OCR error in the second variable's unit label.", 'pdf_interval': [139, 139]}

PDF 181–225，{'theme': "Center of mass from first moments divided by total mass for a body with continuous density on a bounded closed region. The uniform hemisphere example uses axial symmetry and spherical coordinates. OCR obscures the preceding example's numerical centroid.", 'pdf_interval': [181, 181]}；{'theme': 'Moments of inertia about coordinate axes. The discrete sum of mass times squared perpendicular distance becomes an area or volume integral for continuous density. Worked examples use a uniform semicircular lamina and a uniform sphere.', 'pdf_interval': [181, 183]}

PDF 226–267，{'theme': 'Theory. First-kind surface integration is a limit of sample values weighted by patch areas. Continuity on a smooth surface gives existence, piecewise-smooth surfaces are integrated by adding their pieces, and integrating surface density gives mass. Formula (4-2) reduces a graph integral to its planar projection.', 'pdf_interval': [226, 227]}；{'theme': 'Worked examples. A spherical cap is projected onto a disk and treated in polar coordinates. For the tetrahedron with sloping face x+y+z=1, xyz vanishes on the three coordinate faces, leaving a triangular projection with area factor √3. OCR error obscures parts of the displayed numerical results.', 'pdf_interval': [227, 229]}

PDF 268–310，{'pdf_pages': [268, 272], 'theme': 'Positive-term convergence tests. Limit comparison uses the ratio to a known positive series. A finite limit gives eventual upper domination, while a positive or infinite limit gives eventual lower domination. Ratio and root limits below 1 give convergence, above 1 give divergence, and equal to 1 leave the question open. Comparison with 1/n and 1/n^p supplies the power-decay tests.'}；{'pdf_pages': [272, 275], 'theme': 'Alternating series converge when their term magnitudes decrease monotonically to zero. The even and odd partial sums approach the same limit, and the first omitted magnitude bounds the error. Absolute convergence implies convergence by splitting terms into positive and negative parts. The alternating harmonic series illustrates conditional convergence.'}

PDF 311–367，{'theme': 'Theory. Uniform convergence controls integrated remainders. The termwise differentiation theorem uses uniform convergence of the derivative series, followed by a counterexample showing why the original series alone is insufficient. OCR error obscures the counterexample’s exponents.', 'pdf_interval': [311, 312]}；{'theme': 'Theory. The Weierstrass test gives uniform convergence of power series on closed intervals strictly inside the radius of convergence. The text separately discusses convergent endpoints and proves that termwise differentiation preserves the radius.', 'pdf_interval': [312, 314]}

coverage: PDF 1–48 的初始 OCR 核读及下列完整分段 OCR。开头与卷末、代表字形和图表回查原图。

PDF 49–78，{'theme': 'Transition-radiation photon yield above fixed and fractional energy thresholds. Parts of the yield formulas and numerical examples are illegible.', 'pages': [49, 49]}；{'theme': 'Mean muon stopping power and radiative fluctuations. The iron example places ionization dominance through several hundred GeV and bremsstrahlung and direct pair-production dominance above several TeV.', 'pages': [49, 51]}

PDF 79–108，{'theme': 'Systematic error affects accuracy, random error limits precision, and blunders call for checking the measurement. Significant-figure rules align the reported value with the decimal place of its uncertainty.', 'pdf_interval': [79, 81]}；{'theme': 'Reported scintillation-detector background counts and their interpretation. For repeated measurements of equal precision with random errors that average to zero, the arithmetic mean estimates the underlying value and minimizes the unweighted sum of squared deviations.', 'pdf_interval': [81, 84]}

PDF 109–137，{'theme': 'Energy-loss theory. Bethe–Bloch gives the mean stopping power, with minimum ionization near βγ ≈ 3–4, a relativistic rise, and density-effect flattening. For small energy losses, the text uses a Landau approximation and distinguishes the most probable loss from the mean. OCR error obscures the printed low-speed exponent.', 'pages': [109, 111]}；{'theme': 'Reported comparisons. Fig. 4.1.2 compares gas energy-loss measurements and calculations and labels curves with Allison and Cobb (1980) and a 1954 attribution. Fig. 4.1.3 compares measured Ar–CO₂ pulse heights in arbitrary units with Gaussian and Landau calculations. OCR errors obscure the gas label in Fig. 4.1.2, the 1954 surname, and parts of the plotted axes.', 'pages': [110, 111]}

PDF 138–180，{'pdf_pages': [138, 139], 'theme': 'Proportional counters. The resolution model combines primary-ionization and avalanche-gain fluctuations under an initial independence assumption. The experimental measure is full-energy-peak FWHM divided by peak energy for 5.9 keV X-rays. Positive-ion space charge reduces gain, linearity, and high-rate performance. Efficiency factors into window transmission and absorption in the active gas. Sealing affects shelf life, while quencher decomposition and electrode deposits affect counting life. OCR errors affect the variance and Gaussian conversions, the ion-drift unit, and the rate and lifetime exponents.'}；{'pdf_pages': [139, 140], 'theme': 'Proportional-counter applications. A BF₃ tube detects slow neutrons through charged reaction products that ionize the gas. A windowless flow-through 4π counter continuously renews the gas and places the source inside the chamber for absolute activity measurement. OCR errors obscure some isotope superscripts and source-radiation labels.'}

PDF 181–224，{'theme': 'ALICE TOF design and beam test. Two stacks of five MRPC gaps produce simultaneous avalanches whose induced signals are combined, increasing the available charge at the same applied voltage. OCR corrupts the glass resistivity and gap-unit labels.', 'pdf_pages': [181, 182]}；{'theme': 'STAR TOF design and reported performance. High collision multiplicity motivates small readout pads and low occupancy. The text follows six-gap modules through tray geometry, timing calibration, TPC-track-selected efficiency, and charged-hadron identification using time of flight, path length, and momentum. OCR obscures several design units and intrinsic timing values. The outer-glass thickness also differs between the prose and figure OCR.', 'pdf_pages': [182, 184]}

PDF 225–268，{'theme': 'Double-sided silicon strips use reverse bias for near-full depletion and read both faces for two coordinates. Particle CCDs clock charge toward edge outputs, with serial readout trading speed for spatial resolution.', 'pdf_interval': [225, 226]}；{'theme': 'Book-reported CCD implementations include MIMOSA, XMM-Newton and SLD VXD3. The text gives readout times of 5 ms for the XMM-Newton example and 200 ms for full VXD3 readout, and describes the KEK vertex detector as a plan.', 'pdf_interval': [226, 226]}

PDF 269–311，{'theme': 'Photon readout architectures. Microchannel plates suppress ion feedback with angled channels. Fine-mesh PMTs use crossed-wire or segmented anodes for position readout. PD, APD, CCD, VAPD and IPD designs use different combinations of photoconversion and internal gain. Several gain exponents and table units are OCR errors.', 'pdf_interval': [269, 273]}；{'theme': 'PMT response and gain. Photocathode quantum efficiency depends on wavelength, which motivates matching the photocathode and window to the scintillator. Dynode gain compounds across stages and depends strongly on supply voltage.', 'pdf_interval': [273, 276]}

PDF 312–355，{'theme': 'Cherenkov emission and light yield. The wavelength-band estimate uses a yield proportional to z² sin²θ and the difference of reciprocal wavelength limits. For unit charge and β≈1 over 4,000–7,000 Å, the text gives 0.28 photons/cm in air at 1 atm and 272 photons/cm in acrylic. It discusses weak energy loss, the UV yield versus chromatic broadening tradeoff, prompt emission and linear polarization, then compares Cherenkov radiation with bremsstrahlung and fluorescence.', 'pdf_interval': [312, 314]}；{'theme': 'Detector components and radiator selection. Transparency, low fluorescence, low ionization loss and low dispersion govern the choice of radiator. At fixed temperature and modest gas pressure, n−1 scales with pressure in atm. Silica aerogel fills part of the refractive-index gap between gases and denser media.', 'pdf_interval': [314, 316]}

PDF 356–397，{'pdf_pages': [356, 356], 'theme': 'Chapter 7 bibliography on Cherenkov counters, RICH, DIRC, and experimental applications. One journal pagination range appears malformed in the OCR.'}；{'pdf_pages': [357, 357], 'theme': 'Chapter 7 exercises on Cherenkov thresholds, emission angles, photon and photoelectron yields, conical optics, and particle identification with three threshold counters at 3 GeV/c.'}

PDF 398–444，{'theme': 'Calorimeter framework. Electromagnetic sampling uses alternating absorber and active layers, with lead a common absorber. Hadronic showers combine nuclear cascades with an electromagnetic component. The book gives roughly 5–10 nuclear interaction lengths for about 95% longitudinal containment and discusses invisible energy and partial compensation through uranium fission. OCR error affects the resolution formulas and transverse containment notation.', 'pdf_pages': [398, 399]}；{'theme': 'Muon identification by penetration through thick absorbers, with outer gas tracking matched to central tracks for momentum measurement.', 'pdf_pages': [399, 399]}
